title: Visibility for similarity-search endpoints — dashboards, traces, cost alerts
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Provide comprehensive visibility across similarity-search and reranking endpoints: latency and tail SLOs, detailed trace spans for scorer stages, token-level cost attribution per endpoint, and actionable alerting. This work focuses on endpoint-level dashboards, histogram-based latency slices, end-to-end trace instrumentation spanning SDK->router->scorer->cache, and automated alerts tied to cost and quality regressions.
background: Customers have asked for clearer insight into where time and dollars are spent for retrieval and reranking workloads. Current dashboards show aggregate embedding metrics but do not break down by endpoint variant, cache hit behavior, or scorer model version. Incidents in Q3 revealed blind spots: spinner behavior caused by occasional heavy reranks and misattributed cost for batched scorer requests.
acceptance_criteria: New endpoint dashboard exists that can be filtered by tenant and endpoint name
Latency SLI/SLAs visualized at p50/p95/p99 and by scorer stage (encode, retrieve, score, post-process)
Tracing spans are emitted for SDK->gateway->router->scorer, including cache hit metadata and batch sizes
Cost attribution emitted per request: tokens_used, scorer_model, batch_size, hardware_tier
Alerting policy created: spike in p99 latency (>2x baseline) AND increase in cost per 10k requests (>25%)
Automated smoke test that verifies dashboard metrics update during synthetic traffic
tasks: Instrument scorer code to add explicit spans: encode, fetch-index, similarity-score, aggregation
Emit cost metadata from router: tokens, quantized_bytes, gpu_ms, assigned_pool
Add tags for model_variant, scorer_config, and cache_status to traces and metrics
Build Grafana dashboard with: endpoint selector, latency heatmap, cost waterfall, batch-size distribution
Create alerting playbook with runbook links and escalation steps
Implement synthetic load generator that exercises diversity of endpoints and cache-hit ratios
telemetry_signals: request.latency_ms — histogram with 10ms buckets up to 10s
cost.per_request_usd — derived metric using gpu_ms and token count
dashboards: Endpoint Overview: selector for tenant, endpoint, model_version — shows qps, p50/p95/p99, error rate
Latency Breakdown: stacked bars for encode/retrieve/score/post with per-stage percentiles
Cost Waterfall: display breakdown by kernel_time, gpu_ms, batching overhead, caching savings
Batching Heatmap: frequency of batch sizes over time and correlation with latency
Quality Dashboard: sampling of outputs with relevance scores for recent deployments
tracing_requirements: All scorer RPCs must be traced with parent-id from SDK call
Attach cache metadata: hit|miss, matched_prefix_length, cached_ttl_seconds
Record decision points for fallback model selection with selected_candidate_ids
Span attributes: model_variant, quantization_profile, gpu_type, batch_size
cost_breakdown_requirements: Emit token_count and gpu_ns per request into cost pipeline
Map gpu_ns to USD via current pricing table for dedicated pools
Surface effective cost per 1k requests and per-tenant daily spend on dashboard
Add export to billing reports for top 10 cost-generating endpoints
rollout_plan: Phase 1 — instrumentation + internal dashboards on staging (2 weeks)
Phase 2 — enable tracing and cost metrics for opt-in customers in prod (1 week)
Phase 3 — default rollout and alerts enabled for all customers (gradual 2-week ramp)
Post-rollout — 30-day observation window and adjust alert thresholds
risks: High cardinality from model_variant and endpoint tags may blow up metrics storage — need tag aggregation
Cost metric accuracy depends on timely export of gpu_ns; any lag will skew dashboards
Tracing overhead for high QPS endpoints could add measurable latency; must sample strategically
